The native engine fits models from lavaan-style syntax by maximum likelihood,
with a covariance structure and, when you write intercepts, observed means. This
guide covers the whole workflow in one place: syntax, fitting, inference,
constraints, model comparison, diagnostics and the route to the mediation
objects. For a first look, read
[the five-minute quickstart](native-quickstart.html).

| | |
|---|---|
| **Entry points** | `fit_sem(syntax, data)`; `fit_mediation(model = syntax, engine = "native")` for one mediator |
| **Class returned** | `SEMFit`, then `MediationData`, `SerialMediationData` or `ParallelMediationData` from `extract_mediation()` |
| **Syntax reference** | `?"medfit-syntax"` |
| **Not covered** | latent means, latent products, groups, categorical outcomes, other estimators; see [the limits](#limits) |

```{r}
#| label: setup
library(medfit)
library(generics)
d <- mediation_demo
```

## 1. Syntax

| Statement | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `y ~ x1 + x2` | regression of `y` on `x1` and `x2` |
| `f =~ y1 + y2 + y3` | latent variable `f` measured by indicators |
| `y1 ~~ y2` | covariance; `y1 ~~ y1` is a variance |
| `y ~ a*x` | label a path; equal labels are one parameter |
| `y ~ 0.5*x` | fix a path |
| `start(0.3)*`, `lower(0)*`, `upper(1)*` | starting value, lower and upper bound |
| `ab := a*b` | defined parameter with a delta-method standard error |
| `a == b`, `cp == a*b`, `a*b > 0.1` | equality or inequality constraint on labels, linear or not |
| `y1, y2 ~ x` | comma shorthand (a medfit extension; lavaan reads it differently) |

Exogenous observed variables are fixed at their sample moments by default, as lavaan does with
`fixed.x = TRUE` (fewer parameters, the same structural estimates, a conditional log likelihood);
`fixed_x = FALSE` in `fit_sem()` gives them free variances and covariances instead.
Both sides of a constraint and the right side of a definition
are arithmetic expressions in the labels (`+ - * / ^`, parentheses, `exp`, `log`,
`sqrt`, `abs`, `min`, `max`, `pnorm`, `qnorm`, and a few more).

## 2. Fit and read

```{r}
#| label: fit
syntax <- "
  mediator1 ~ a * treatment + covariate1
  outcome ~ b * mediator1 + cp * treatment + covariate1
  ab := a * b
  total := cp + a * b
"
fit <- fit_sem(syntax, d)
summary(fit)
```

| To get | Use |
|---|---|
| free-parameter estimates | `coef(fit)`; names are the label, else `lhs op rhs` without spaces (`M~X`, `eta=~m2`), as `lavaan::coef()` |
| the covariance matrix | `vcov(fit)` |
| a table with intervals | `tidy(fit, conf_int = TRUE)`; `confint(fit)` for the matrix |
| defined parameters | `fit@defined`, or the `:=` rows of `tidy()` and `confint()` |
| chi-square, df, logLik, AIC, BIC | `glance(fit)`; `logLik(fit)`, `nobs(fit)` |

```{r}
#| label: tidy
tidy(fit, conf_int = TRUE)[, c("term", "estimate", "std_error", "conf_low", "conf_high")]
glance(fit)
```

The chi-square is $n$ times the minimized discrepancy and has `df` degrees of
freedom. A saturated model (here `df = 0`) fits perfectly by construction, so the
test only means something when there are restrictions.

## 3. Standard errors and weights

The default information matrix is observed; `information = "expected"` gives
lavaan's default. `se_type = "sandwich"` gives the HC0 robust covariance, and
`weights` takes case weights.

```{r}
#| label: se
w <- seq_len(nrow(d)) %% 3 + 1
robust <- fit_sem(syntax, d, weights = w, se_type = "sandwich")
rbind(model_based = sqrt(diag(vcov(fit)))[1:3], weighted_robust = sqrt(diag(vcov(robust)))[1:3])
```

## 4. Constraints

A constraint is a line of syntax. The engine classifies it and uses the cheapest
exact route:

| Constraint | Example | How it is solved |
|---|---|---|
| linear equality or bound | `a == b`, `a + b == 1`, `a < 0.3` | constant Jacobian rows; every accepted solution passes a gate on all rows |
| nonlinear equality | `cp == a*b` | Jacobian recomputed at every point; every start tried, the best accepted one kept; a Newton polish after acceptance |
| nonlinear inequality | `a*b > 0.1`, `ab > 0` with `ab := a*b` | same, as rows $c(\theta) \le 0$; a warning when the starts disagree |
| one independent nonzero product | `a*b == 0.1` | both sign domains searched; an unresolved required branch stops the fit; coverage is not global optimality |
| product set to zero | `a*b == 0`, `b1*b2*b3 == 0` | exact: one linear fit per factor, smallest discrepancy kept |
| sum of products | `a1*b1 + a2*b2 == 0` | best-effort: the best of the starts; a disagreement warning means a better optimum may exist, so raise `n_starts` |

```{r}
#| label: constraints
tied <- fit_sem(paste0(syntax, "cp == a * b\n"), d)
round(coef(tied)[c("a", "b", "cp")], 4)
tied@diagnostics$active_constraints
```

Labels used in a constraint must be defined in the model, and a constraint with
no free parameter is an error. `CONSTRAINT(a == b)` is the same as the bare
`a == b`.

## 5. Compare models and test the indirect effect

`anova()` is the likelihood-ratio test for nested `SEMFit`s; it refits nothing.
Nesting is checked by parameter-table inclusion, a necessary condition, so
two models that pass but are not nested in substance are your responsibility. `mbco_sem()` tests an indirect
effect that is a product of paths:

```{r}
#| label: compare
anova(tied, fit)
mbco_sem(fit, "a", "b")
```

For a chain `a`, `d`, `b`, give the paths: `mbco_sem(fit, paths = c("a", "d", "b"))`
is the minimum of the single-path tests against a chi-square with one degree of
freedom. The null is a union of hypotheses, so the test is conservative when more
than one path is zero (its size is at most 0.055 at the 5% level in the package's
simulation gate).

## 6. Diagnostics

Read these before trusting a fit; all are in `summary(fit)` and `fit@diagnostics`:

| Field | What it says | If it is wrong |
|---|---|---|
| `Converged` | the optimizer returned and the acceptance gate passed | the fit is not returned; the error names the failure |
| `Optimizer status`, `stationarity` | the solver's code and the Newton decrement at the solution | a large decrement means a stall; try `n_starts` |
| `Active bounds` / `Active constraints` | which bounds or constraints bind | a binding bound means the estimate is on the edge |
| `Improper solution` | a negative variance or non-positive definite covariance | respecify, or bound the variance |
| `Multiplier sign check` | active inequality multipliers have the right sign | a wrong sign means an active bound was not optimal |

```{r}
#| label: bound
b <- fit_sem(paste0(syntax, "outcome ~~ lower(2) * outcome\n"), d)
b@diagnostics$active_bounds
```

For the nonzero-product supported shapes, local-search limits and coverage record, see
[the constraints page](model-native-constraints.html#nonzero-product-equality).

When a model with a nonlinear constraint warns that the starts reached different
optima, the constraint has more than one solution (`a*b > 0.1` holds for two
positive or two negative paths). The kept fit is the best, but say so in a report.

### The outcome ledger {#the-outcome-ledger}

Every native fit keeps a versioned record of how it was reached, `fit@diagnostics$ledger`: one node per fit,
zero-product branch and `mbco_sem()` null, each with its optimizer state, likelihood, covariance status and
notices. A node is `resolved` (the optimizer accepted it) or `unresolved`, and `unresolved` means unknown: only a
`feasibility` of `certified_empty` is a proof that a branch has no solution, and only a literal contradiction such
as `a == 0` with `a == 1` earns it. Errors that stop a fit carry the same ledger as `$ledger`, and `mbco_sem()` and
`compare_lr()` return it with an unresolved result. Read it with `str(fit@diagnostics$ledger, max.level = 2)`;
the cases and what to do are in [Troubleshooting](guide-troubleshooting.html#errors-that-carry-evidence), and the
construction is in [Computation and algorithms](computation-algorithms.html#a-zero-product-is-a-union-of-simpler-models).

## 7. From a fit to mediation objects

```{r}
#| label: extract
x <- extract_mediation(fit, treatment = "treatment", mediator = "mediator1",
                       outcome = "outcome")
class(x)[1]
```

`fit_mediation(model = syntax, engine = "native", treatment =, mediator =)` does
both steps for **one** mediator. For several mediators, fit with `fit_sem()` and call
`extract_mediation(fit, mediator = c("m1", "m2"), outcome = )`: a chain gives a
`SerialMediationData`, mediators side by side a `ParallelMediationData`. A latent
mediator works through the same call.

## Limits {#limits}

- **Observed means only.** Intercepts (`y ~ 1`, `y ~ 1 + x`) are estimated for observed variables;
  a free latent mean or intercept stops with "latent means are planned for a later release".
- **One group**, listwise deletion for missing data, **numeric variables only**.
- **ML only**, plus the HC0 sandwich; no robust chi-square, no fit indices beyond
  the chi-square, AIC and BIC.
- **Products** (`x:m`, which give the four-way decomposition) work for two observed variables inside a
  supported class; the table of limits and messages is on [the native model page](model-native.html#product-terms).
  The model test is `NA` when a product factor is a regression target.
- **AIC and BIC of a fit with a product are not comparable** with those of a fit without one (the product
  column enters the likelihood), so `AIC(fit_a, fit_b)` and `BIC()` refuse such a pair; see
  [the native model page](model-native.html#limits).
- For latent means, groups, categorical outcomes or fit indices use lavaan; the extraction
  route accepts a `lavaan` fit as well. See
  [lavaan and the native engine](lavaan-comparison.html).

## Bounded FIML (unreleased) {#bounded-fiml}

This separate development milestone is not assigned to 0.16 and is unavailable
in released 0.15.0. Ordinary calls still delete incomplete model rows listwise.
The explicit opt-in below fits exactly three numeric continuous observed
variables: X to M to Y with a free or exactly zero direct path, independent
Gaussian disturbances and free intercepts. It assumes ignorable missingness
under that joint model; FIML does not impute the missing values.

```{r}
#| label: bounded-fiml-workflow
fiml_data <- mediation_demo[c("treatment", "mediator1", "outcome")]
fiml_data$mediator1[seq(1, nrow(fiml_data), by = 7)] <- NA_real_
fiml_syntax <- "mediator1 ~ a*treatment
outcome ~ b*mediator1 + cp*treatment"
fiml_fit <- medfit::fit_sem(
  fiml_syntax, fiml_data, missing = "fiml", fixed_x = FALSE,
  meanstructure = TRUE, information = "observed", se_type = "model"
)
c(retained_rows = nobs(fiml_fit), logLik = as.numeric(logLik(fiml_fit)))
fiml_effects <- extract_mediation(fiml_fit, treatment = "treatment", mediator = "mediator1")
nie(fiml_effects)
nde(fiml_effects)
te(fiml_effects)
tidy(fiml_effects, type = "effects")
```

The wrapper route is `fit_mediation(model = fiml_syntax, data = fiml_data,
treatment = "treatment", mediator = "mediator1", engine = "native",
se_type = "model", engine_args = list(missing = "fiml", fixed_x = FALSE,
meanstructure = TRUE, information = "observed"))`. There is no new top-level
`missing` argument on `fit_mediation()`; `med()` remains a formula-building fitter.
The missing-method strings must match exactly. A failed FIML fit never falls
back to listwise deletion or another engine, even on complete data.

| Setting | Bounded FIML requirement |
| --- | --- |
| `fixed_x` | Explicit `FALSE`; omission, `TRUE` and named subsets refuse |
| `meanstructure` | `TRUE`; `NULL` and `FALSE` refuse |
| `information`, `se_type` | `"observed"`, `"model"` |
| Weights | No non-NULL vector, including unit weights or the deprecated alias |
| `n_starts`, `control` | `NULL` or 3; empty control; no syntax-supplied starts |
| Topology | Three variables only; free or exactly zero direct path; no `:=`, constraints, ties, bounds, extra predictors, latent variables, factors or products |

The start/control restrictions preserve the initial validated protocol, rather
than expressing mathematical limits of FIML. Three starts run for each solver;
six attempt groups normally involve nine actual calls with nlminb refinements.
Failures and completed calls are retained separately. Numerical acceptance
requires both solvers, stationarity, agreeing likelihoods, local rank and valid
observed information; it does not certify a global optimum or inference coverage.

Rows with any observed model variable are retained, including singleton patterns;
only all-empty model rows are dropped. Extra columns do not select rows. No
complete-case initialization is used: data with no complete rows can fit when
local identification checks pass. `nobs()` counts retained rows, not observed
cells. Original positional row IDs and pattern/count evidence are retained.

`coef()`, full `vcov()`, `nobs()`, raw `logLik()`, AIC/BIC, print/summary,
parameter tidy and normal confidence intervals work on the SEMFit. Its
`glance()` reports likelihood/IC fields, with model-test fields unavailable and
an explicit reason. The discrepancy `f` and model-test `df` are `NA`; the separate
free-parameter count is eight or nine. There is no saturated missing-data fit.
See [Methods and Formulas](methods.html#bounded-fiml) for the likelihood.

Extraction preserves validated FIML context through copying and serialization.
Original SEMFit labels/full covariance stay unchanged; extracted a/b/c_prime
and m_/y_ aliases follow topology, with original coordinates retained in context.
Supported extracted operations are `paths()`, `nie()`, `nde()`, `te()`, `coef()`
(paths/effects/all), full `vcov()`, print/summary, tidy and normal path/effect
confidence intervals. At a = b = 0 the NIE point value is retained but its
inferential fields are unavailable. A fixed direct path of zero instead has
known zero covariance; other valid effect inference remains available.

Extracted-object `glance()`, `quick()`, `pm()`, bootstrap/boot intervals, profiles,
MBCO, fit tests, fit indices and prediction/residual APIs are deferred and refuse
FIML objects. Package object-aware guards act before package-controlled refits,
RNG or worker launch; opaque user callbacks are outside this guarantee. AIC/BIC
comparisons dispatched with SEMFit first require compatible FIML contexts and
refuse external/mixed objects before external likelihood calls. Calls dispatched
first through another class are outside medfit's guard.
